newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Ursus confirms Agco bid.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Ursus confirms Agco bid.

text.p: U.S. farm equipment maker Agco Corp has bid to buy Polish state-owned tractor maker ZM Ursus, Ursus general manager said on Tuesday.
"Agco has placed, as the only company, a written offer for the entire Ursus company," Janusz Sciskalski said.

On Monday, Agco chairman Robert Ratliff told the Financial Times in an interview that his company was ready to spend $1.5 billion on acquisitions of European farm equipment makers and listed Ursus among possible takeover targets.

Sciskalski said several other companies were interested in the state-owned Ursus, which in June underwent a 600-million zloty debt restructuring scheme, but only Agco wanted to buy the whole firm while other investors eyed only its particular units.
But he also said Ursus management favoured a plan to split up the company into three parts: tractor, metallurgy and trading divisions and sell them separately to different investors.
"I hope that such a solution is finally chosen and that we will have a piecemeal privatisation," Sciskalski said.
He said Ursus, the country's largest tractor maker, could be ready for privatisation in mid-1997.
